title: Does a generalized quadrangle of order (4,12) exist?
credit: Open problem in Payne–Thas, Finite Generalized Quadrangles; SRG status from A. E. Brouwer's tables.
premise_risks: Two-case question; could be split into GQ(4,11) and GQ(4,12) separately
Could not locate a 2024-2026 source that explicitly restates 'GQ(4,11), GQ(4,12) open', status inferred from Brouwer's live SRG table (point graphs open) and Payne–Thas
plain: A generalized quadrangle of order (s,t) is a point-line geometry in which every line has s+1 points, every point is on t+1 lines, two points share at most one line, and for every point P not on a line L exactly one point of L is collinear with P. For five points per line (s=4), the standard counting conditions allow t in {1,2,4,6,8,11,12,16}, and all but t=11 and t=12 are realised. Decide whether such a quadrangle exists for t=12 (the case t=11 is a separate problem).
math: For t = 12 only: decide whether there exists a finite incidence structure with nonempty point set, every line of size 5, every point on exactly 13 lines, two distinct lines meeting in at most one point, and for every P not on L exactly one Q on L collinear with P. (Case t = 11 is posed as a separate problem with the same definitions.)
